q: Raja Rammohan Roy, often called the 'father of Indian Renaissance', founded the Atmiya Sabha in 1814 with the aim of:
o: Propagating the monotheistic ideals of the Vedanta and campaigning against idolatry and caste rigidities
Reviving Vedic education exclusively for Brahmins
Establishing a purely political organisation against the British
Promoting the Sharia among Bengal Muslims

q: Keshab Chandra Sen was dismissed as acharya of the Brahmo Samaj in 1865 mainly because of his:
o: Refusal to accept the doctrine of monotheism
Radical views such as cosmopolitanisation of worship and support for inter-caste marriages, opposed by Debendranath Tagore
Opposition to widow remarriage
Support for sati

q: Which of the following is cited as a key reason for the limited long-term impact of the Derozians (Young Bengal Movement)?
o: They focused exclusively on economic issues and ignored social reform
They had strong support from the peasantry but lacked intellectual leadership
Their radicalism was largely bookish and lacked real links with the masses, including failure to take up the peasants' cause
They were suppressed violently by the British government

q: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, as principal of Sanskrit College from 1850, is notable for:
o: Opening the Sanskrit College to non-Brahmins to break the priestly monopoly of scriptural knowledge
Founding the Arya Samaj
Establishing the Theosophical Society in India
Leading the Wahabi Movement

q: The Paramahansa Mandali, founded in 1849 in Maharashtra by Dadoba Pandurang and Mehtaji Durgaram, is particularly notable for its members':
o: Alliance with orthodox Dharma Sabha
Rejection of widow remarriage as un-Hindu
Practice of taking food cooked by lower-caste people at their meetings to break caste rules
Insistence on strict vegetarianism as an article of faith

q: Jyotiba Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (Truth Seekers' Society) in 1873, drawing its leadership mainly from:
o: British-educated civil servants
Wealthy zamindars and moneylenders
Backward classes such as malis, telis, kunbis, saris and dhangars
Brahmin scholars and priests

q: Which of Jyotiba Phule's works used the symbol of Raja Bali, as opposed to the Brahminical symbol of Rama, to inspire the common masses?
o: Tahdhib-ul-Akhlaq
Gulamgiri and Sarvajanik Satyadharma
Precepts of Jesus
Satyarth Prakash

q: Gopalhari Deshmukh, known by his pen name 'Lokahitawadi', is remembered for the statement:
o: "Educate, Agitate, Organise."
"As many faiths, so many paths."
"If religion does not sanction social reform, then change religion."
"Back to the Vedas."

q: The Servants of India Society, founded in 1905 by Gopal Krishna Gokhale with the help of M.G. Ranade, aimed to:
o: Focus exclusively on temple entry issues in South India
Directly lead the Indian National Congress
Train national missionaries devoted to selfless service of the country while staying aloof from political organisations like the INC
Organise armed resistance against British rule

q: Narayan Malhar Joshi, a follower of Gokhale, founded the Social Service League in Bombay and later also founded which major labour organisation in 1920?
o: Servants of India Society
Justice Movement
Self-Respect Movement
All India Trade Union Congress

q: The Ramakrishna Mission, founded by Swami Vivekananda in 1897 to fulfil the second objective of the Ramakrishna movement, has its headquarters (along with the Ramakrishna Math) at:
o: Adyar, Madras
Aligarh
Belur, near Calcutta
Lahore

q: At the Parliament of Religions held in Chicago in 1893, Swami Vivekananda's keynote address emphasised:
o: The necessity of converting Western audiences to Hinduism
The need for a healthy balance between spiritualism and materialism, blending Western materialism with Eastern spiritualism
A rejection of all Western scientific and technological advances
The exclusive superiority of Hinduism over all other world religions

q: Which of the following distinguishes the Ramakrishna Mission from the Arya Samaj, as noted in the chapter?
o: The Ramakrishna Mission recognises the utility and value of image worship, unlike the Arya Samaj which rejected idolatry
The Ramakrishna Mission was founded before the Arya Samaj
The Ramakrishna Mission rejected the Vedas while the Arya Samaj upheld them
The Arya Samaj was founded by Vivekananda

q: The Arya Samaj split in 1893 primarily over differences regarding the curriculum of which institution, leading to the College Party and the Mahatma (Gurukul) Party?
o: Fergusson College, Poona
Aligarh's Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College
Darul Uloom, Deoband
Dayananda Anglo-Vedic (D.A.V.) College, Lahore

q: Swami Shraddhanand (Lala Munshi Ram), leader of the Mahatma/Gurukul faction of the Arya Samaj, established the Gurukul Kangri near Haridwar after initially founding a gurukul in 1900 at:
o: Gujaranwala, West Punjab
Lahore
Deoband
Aligarh

q: The shuddhi (purification) movement launched by the Arya Samaj aimed to:
o: Convert Hindus to Christianity
Establish separate Muslim educational institutions
Promote inter-religious marriages between Hindus and Muslims
Reconvert Christian and Muslim converts back to the Hindu fold and uplift those regarded as untouchables into caste Hindu status

q: The Seva Sadan, founded in 1908 by the Parsi reformer B.M. Malabari along with Diwan Dayaram Gidumal, primarily served:
o: Orphaned children of freedom fighters
Muslim peasants displaced by indigo planters
Exploited and discarded women, providing education, medical and welfare services across castes
Widowed Brahmin men seeking remarriage

q: The Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana (SNDP) movement, launched among the Ezhavas of Kerala, is associated with which symbolic act performed by Narayana Guru at Aruvippuram in 1888?
o: Burning the Manusmriti in public
Installing a stone taken from the Neyyar river as a Sivalinga, asserting that idol consecration was not the monopoly of higher castes
Founding the Ezhava Memorial demanding job reservation
Leading a satyagraha to open the Vaikom temple roads

q: The temple entry movement of 1931, in which poet Subramaniyam Tirumambu (the 'singing sword of Kerala') led volunteers to Guruvayur, culminated in which proclamation of 1936?
o: The Age of Consent Act raising the marriage age
The Maharaja of Travancore's proclamation opening all government-controlled temples to all Hindus
The Sikh Gurudwaras Act transferring gurudwara control to the SGPC
The Government of India Act's provision for reserved seats

q: The Indian Social Conference, founded by M.G. Ranade and Raghunath Rao, functioned effectively as:
o: A purely religious organisation with no social agenda
The social reform cell of the Indian National Congress, meeting annually at the same venue as the INC
An exclusively Muslim reform body
A rival political party to the Congress

q: The Wahabi/Walliullah Movement, inspired by Shah Walliullah's teachings, initially directed its activities against the Sikhs in Punjab, but after 1849 turned its focus against:
o: The Marathas
The Aligarh Movement
The Deoband ulema
The British, following the British annexation of Punjab

q: Titu Mir (Mir Nithar Ali), a disciple of Syed Ahmed Barelvi, organised Muslim peasants of Bengal chiefly against:
o: Wahabi missionaries
The Faraizi leadership
Hindu landlords and British indigo planters
The Aligarh Movement

q: The Ahmadiyya Movement, founded by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad in 1889, is distinctive among Islamic sects for its belief that:
o: Jihad against non-Muslims is a fundamental religious duty
India must be converted into dar-ul-Islam by force
The Messiah had come in the person of Mirza Ghulam Ahmad to end religious wars and reinstate morality
The four schools of Muslim jurisprudence should remain separate

q: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan opposed active political participation by Muslims in the immediate term mainly because:
o: He wanted Muslims to join the Wahabi Movement instead
He believed Muslims should first focus on education and employment before engaging in politics to avoid inviting government hostility
He believed Islam forbade any political engagement with a non-Muslim government
He supported the Indian National Congress's political programme fully

q: The Deoband Movement, founded at the Darul Uloom in Saharanpur district in 1866 by Mohammad Qasim Nanotavi and Rashid Ahmed Gangohi, differed from the Aligarh Movement in that it:
o: Welcomed British patronage and supported Syed Ahmed Khan's organisations
Rejected the formation of the Indian National Congress
Aimed at moral and religious regeneration of Muslims through original Islamic education, rather than Western education and government support
Advocated exclusively for Western scientific curricula

q: The Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha (1851), a Parsi reform association whose leaders included Dadabhai Naoroji and Naoroji Furdonji, aimed at:
o: Regeneration of Parsi social conditions and restoration of Zoroastrian religion to its pristine purity
Founding a new syncretic religion combining Hinduism and Zoroastrianism
Establishing Islamic law among the Parsi community
Converting Parsis to Christianity

q: The Singh Sabha Movement, founded at Amritsar in 1873, had which two-fold objective?
o: Spreading modern Western education among Sikhs and countering the proselytising activities of Christian, Brahmo, Arya Samaj and Muslim missionaries
Establishing a separate Sikh state and abolishing the SGPC
Merging Sikhism with the Arya Samaj
Promoting the Wahabi ideology among Sikhs

q: The Theosophical Society, founded in New York in 1875 by Madame H.P. Blavatsky and Colonel M.S. Olcott, shifted its headquarters in 1882 to:
o: Belur, near Calcutta
Adyar, on the outskirts of Madras
Aligarh
Lahore

q: Annie Besant, who became president of the Theosophical Society after Olcott's death in 1907, laid the foundation of the Central Hindu College at Benaras in 1898, which later became the nucleus for:
o: Aligarh Muslim University
Fergusson College
Gurukul Kangri
Benaras Hindu University (1916)

q: Which of the following is identified as a major limitation (negative aspect) of the 19th-20th century socio-religious reform movements as a whole?
o: Their exclusive focus on economic issues at the expense of social reform
Their complete failure to address the position of women
Their narrow social base, being confined largely to the educated urban middle classes while ignoring the peasantry and urban poor
Their total rejection of religious authority and tradition
